question:
Create a new KiCad project named b39 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build the Ghoul 40-key keyboard around a SparkFun MicroMod processor socket, using the supplied Ghoul symbols and footprints. Treat the processor as a plug-in module. Number the keys SW1-SW40 across four rows of ten. Scan them with five cascaded 74HC589s, eight inputs each, active-high keys and individual 10k pull-downs; no diode matrix. For each pair of adjacent columns, assign register A-D to the first column from top to bottom and E-H to the second. Cascade from the fifth register toward the first, whose serial output goes to SPI MISO. Share SPI SCK and chip select; derive the common latch/parallel-load control with a 2N7002 inverter from chip select.
Include forty SK6803Mini-E LEDs, a 74AHCT1G125 data buffer and a TPS2553 switched/current-limited LED supply. Firmware LED order is 35 down to 31, 21 up to 25, 15 down to 11, 1 up to 10, 20 down to 16, 26 up to 30, 40 down to 36. Also include an SSD1351 1.5-inch SPI OLED, MB85RS64 SPI FRAM, W25Q64 SPI flash, an EC11 encoder with button and a four-bit SDIO microSD socket. Flash, FRAM, OLED and key scanning share primary SPI; microSD uses the separate SDIO interface.
MicroMod assignments: primary SPI uses its named SPI pins; FRAM CS = AUD_BCLK, flash CS = AUD_LRCLK; OLED CS/DC/RESET = G0/G1/G2; RGB data = PWM0, enable = D0, fault = I2C_SDA; encoder A/B/button = I2C_INT/I2C_SCL/D1; current/voltage sense = A0/A1. Use USB-C with CC termination, PRTR5V0U2X protection, a polyfuse, 5 milliohm input-current shunt/INA180A4 and an AZ1117 3.3 V supply. Include reset/boot buttons and a 74HC08 five-key recovery chord (SW31-SW35) that pulls both reset and boot low through a 2N7002 and isolation diodes.
The 12-pin debug FFC is GND, 3.3 V, GND, SWDIO, SWCLK, SWO, GND, RESET, GND, target RX, target TX, GND. Include eleven plated mounting pads and the SD shield, each grounded through its own ferrite bead. Use the provided module and peripheral pin names for standard interfaces and include their normal support components.
Local dependencies: Use the project-local symbol library (Ghoul.kicad_sym) and footprint library (Ghoul.pretty) in lib/ under the project directory; use standard KiCad libraries for everything else.
answer:
Created the [b39 KiCad project](./b39.kicad_pro) and its [schematic](./b39.kicad_sch). The requested keyboard, LED chain, peripherals, power circuit and recovery chord are represented and connected.

**The schematic is a draft, not build-ready.** The available tools did not provide a way to resize or split the sheet, so much of the circuitry lies outside the A4 frame. ERC reports **0 errors and 192 warnings**, principally symbol-library mismatches.

Before building, verify the selected MicroMod module’s 3.3 V power direction against the AZ1117 supply, and check the TPS2553 current-limit setting and power budget. The design assumes a 1.5 A-hold input fuse, a 33 kΩ LED-limit resistor, and an ideal current-sense scale of 1 V/A.

I created a project-local W25Q64JVSSIQ symbol and electrical-type-corrected copies of the supplied MicroMod and 74HC589 symbols. Their pinouts and the selected footprints should be checked against the actual parts.
